key_findings: Resolved the real FLoRA reproduction node (OSF x9pd3, SCORE project dtnq9); obtained raw author Study-2 data (study 2 data.xlsx, n=102), the bushel claims inventory, ADR criteria record, and the human transparency trail.

Headline claim 1 (enjoyment): recomputed independent-samples t-test -> commercial group M=5.38 (SD 1.69, n=53) vs no-commercial M=4.47 (SD 2.05, n=49); t(100)=2.45 (Welch t=2.43), p=0.016. Reproduces the paper's M=5.38 vs 4.47, t(100)=2.43, p=.016 (means exact; t differs only in 2nd decimal due to software precision).
Headline claim 2 (log-transformed willingness to pay): t(100)=2.00, p=0.048; unadjusted WTP means $5.42 vs $4.18. Reproduces exactly on rounding.

The human analyst (Martončik) declared the flagship enjoyment claim 'did not reproduce' ONLY because their precise criterion required t=2.43 to exactly match, whereas recomputation yields t=2.45; all three primary outcomes (n=102, p=.016, means) match otherwise. Substantively the headline is reproduced.

Registry metadata mismatch (cosmetic): study listed as 'Enhancing the Taste of Beer' but the actual DOI 10.1086/597030 / reproduction is 'Enhancing the Television-Viewing Experience through Commercial Interruptions' (JCR 2009).
notes: Raw author data reproduced all focal Study-2 claims (focal enjoyment t-test and the log-WTP secondary claim). No analysis code was deposited inside the reproduction node (script linked separately at osf.io/4jng5) and the raw file required manual deletion of 3 trailing text rows ('Test Relative Preference:/Test WTP:') for recovery of the 102 valid cases - minor computational friction consistent with the human 'computational issues' flag. Only Study 2 (the single-trace focal claim) was verifiable from shared data; the paper's other 5 studies were not independently re-runnable from this package. Verdict: numerical results reproduce (CONSISTENT); the 'computational issues' human label reflects exact-statistic rounding and data-cleaning friction rather than a substantive failure.
